scenes.text: Type a sentence, like a tiger riding a scooter in Hyderabad, and seconds later, you have a picture. [1] Nobody drew it, and it never existed before. [2] So let's understand how AI creates images, with diffusion.

Most image generators use something called diffusion. [1] And the idea is surprisingly simple. The AI learns to turn random noise into a clear picture, step by step. [2] It starts with pure static, [3] removes a little noise at each step, [4] until a picture appears.

data.definition: An AI that learns to turn random noise into a clear image, one small step at a time.

scenes.text: So how does it learn this? [1] During training, it takes millions of real images, and adds noise to them, bit by bit, until they're pure static. [2] Then it practises the reverse, predicting and removing that noise at every step. [3] And after enough practice, it can start from fresh static, and create a brand new image.

scenes.text: So where does your sentence come in? [1] You type your prompt. [2] A text model turns it into numbers that capture its meaning, just like embeddings. [3] The image model starts from random static, [4] and at every step, it removes noise in the direction of your description, [5] until your tiger on a scooter appears.

data.heading: From words to picture
nodes: Each step moves toward your words

scenes.text: Here are four words you'll see in image tools. [1] The prompt, which is your description. [2] The seed, the starting static, so the same seed gives a similar image. [3] Steps, how many rounds of clean-up, where more steps usually means more detail. [4] And the negative prompt, which says what you don't want, like blurry, or extra fingers.

So where is it used? [1] Designers create posters, ads and social media visuals in minutes. [2] Game and film teams sketch concept art and storyboards. [3] And online shops create product photos, without a photo shoot.

Here's a common myth. [1] People think AI image generators just copy and paste bits of existing pictures. [2] That's not how diffusion works. It learns patterns, like what a tiger or a scooter looks like, and builds a new image from noise. But questions about training data and copyright are real, and we'll cover them in a later episode.

data.myth: AI image generators copy and paste bits of existing pictures.
data.fact: Diffusion learns patterns and builds a new image from noise. Training-data questions are still real.
